why: A release bundle embeds its frontend, needs no development server, and is the path an actual user takes, so this is the representative measurement for the ten-second first-terminal goal. Note that not every debug build behaves this way: pnpm tauri build --debug also embeds the frontend, while a bare cargo build loads build.devUrl and would render a blank window here.

remote.fixture: ephemeral isolated HOME + localhost OpenSSH sshd, key authentication

limitations: The remote round-trip uses a preseeded localhost key-authenticated workspace; it does not prove first-user host selection, password/agent/jump authentication, or WAN latency.
The shell prompt is rendered on the xterm canvas and stays diagnostic-only through AX; local PTY and shell-interaction probes prove interactivity separately.
The bundle is unsigned and unnotarized, so Gatekeeper launch behaviour on a clean machine is not covered here.
Human physical keyboard, real macOS IME, Option/dead key, Windows OpenSSH Agent/Pageant/ConPTY, and serial hardware acceptance remain unverified.

superseded.reason: An earlier run of this scenario measured a previous release binary (3ef36d97…) at 3219ms local and 1646ms remote. Because the runners relink target/release/terminal on every build, that binary no longer exists on disk and its numbers cannot be reproduced or compared against the current release SSH matrix.
